summary: A tight, tense bidding game where players spend from a shared, shrinking pool of cash cards to acquire luxury cards or avoid disaster cards, all while knowing the poorest player at the end is disqualified from winning. Every bid is a real trade-off between building a score and having enough cash left to stay in contention, which makes even a 15-20 minute game feel sharp and painful.
praised: Elegant, minimalist design with almost no rules overhead
Constant nail-biting tension despite the short playtime
The 'poorest player is disqualified' twist forces genuinely hard bidding decisions
Plays fast and scales well across its player count
Highly replayable due to variable card draw order
criticised: Can feel like a 'take that' bluffing/psychology exercise more than a strategic game to some
Luck of card order can swing outcomes
Very light theme pasted onto an abstract bidding mechanism
Not much to do beyond bidding, so repeated plays can feel samey to some groups

interaction.kind: Simultaneous-ish turn-order bidding and bluffing over a shared resource pool

win_criteria: Most points, one or two sources

scoring.why: The winner is whoever has the highest total of acquired number/multiplier cards among players who did not end with the least money.
